title: DFS in Alfama: Can You Reach the Viewpoint?
description: Watch DFS explore Lisbon’s Alfama street layout by diving deep along paths until it hits dead ends, then backtracking to try alternatives. This visualization turns real-world map connectivity into a graph-search lesson you can feel in real time.
ig_caption:
🧭✨ **DFS in Lisbon (Alfama)** — go deep, backtrack smart.

In this reel, **Depth-First Search (DFS)** walks the street-map graph by repeatedly choosing a next neighbor and pushing forward until it can’t go further, then **backtracks** to explore other branches. In graph theory terms, DFS traverses vertices in a way that builds a **DFS search tree/forest**, marking visited nodes to avoid cycles and ensure the exploration remains correct on real street connectivity.

🗺️ We treat streets/intersections as a graph: **nodes = crossings**, **edges = traversable segments**. Even on winding districts like Alfama, DFS reveals how traversal order changes the path you see—because DFS focuses on depth over shortest distance.

👉 Want to try a different behavior? Comment **“BFS vs DFS”** and I’ll visualize both on the same map next! 💬
